gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Redtiger F17's parking monitor works only with a hardwire kit that is not in the box, and then records either at 1 fps for 12 or 24 hours or stays off until a jolt wakes it.
standout_why: Compared against productbible.com (cited), dattatecblog.com (cited) and us.my-best.com (cited); vortexradar.com (cited) returned HTTP 403 and was not read. dattatecblog gives the F17 3CH only 'Dual parking mode options' with no hardwire requirement, though it says 'hardwire kit sold separately' for sibling Redtiger models, and ChatGPT's own answer already warns a kit may cost extra. productbible already lists the Vantrue N4S at 1944p + 1440p + 1440p at 30 fps with 10-second buffered motion parking. None of the three pages says resolution or frame rate changes when all channels record, and none gives the F17's 1 fps or off-until-jolt parking behaviour or its 256 GB card ceiling. So rivals hold the general half (kit sold separately) and lack the F17-specific half. I scored it 1, not 2, because the Vantrue side of the contrast is not maker-sourced: vantrue.com returned HTTP 429 on every attempt.
decides: It confirms the F17 for a shopper who only wants driving footage: the F17 manual lists Front 4K + Inside 1080P + Rear 1080P as a three-channel mode. It weakens the F17 for the '24/7 parking surveillance' shopper ChatGPT asks about: plugged into the 12 V socket it has no parking monitor at all, and with the separately bought kit it gives a 1 fps time-lapse or a camera that is off until hit. productbible credits the N4S with 10-second buffered motion parking, which would make it the parking pick if the maker's page bears that out and its price stays at or under $200. The F17 manual also lists a third resolution option, 'Front2.5K+Inside2.5K/Front4K+Rear1080P', which names only two cameras per option; that suggests the cabin camera rises above 1080P only with the rear camera off, but the manual does not say so outright.
